GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2022-05-03T22:29:43Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: CS0539 implementing interface method with T? explicitly
Description: **Version Used**:  NET6

Getting a strange CS0539 error trying to implement an interface method explicitly. Not sure if this is by-design, thought I would ask.

(Nullable context enabled in this scenario.)

Consider these two interfaces:

```csharp
internal interface Interface1
{
	void Method<T>(T value);
}

internal interface Interface2
{
	void MethodNullable<T>(T? value);
}
```

`Interface2` differs in that it has `T?`. My goal is to accept `T`, `null`, or `Nullable<T>`.

These interfaces both work fine when implemented directly/implicitly(?):

```csharp
internal sealed class TestClass : Interface1, Interface2
{
	public void Method<T>(T value) { }

	public void MethodNullable<T>(T? value) { }
}
```

But for some reason `Interface2.MethodNullable` generates CS0539 when implemented explicitly:

```csharp
internal sealed class TestClassExplicit : Interface1, Interface2
{
	void Interface1.Method<T>(T value) { }

	// Generates CS0539
	void Interface2.MethodNullable<T>(T? value) { }
}
```

**Expected Behavior**:

No errors.

**Actual Behavior**:

* `CS0535 'TestClassExplicit' does not implement interface member 'Interface2.MethodNullable<T>(T?)'`
* `CS0539 'TestClassExplicit.MethodNullable<T>(T?)' in explicit interface declaration is not found among members of the interface that can be implemented`
* `CS0453 The type 'T' must be a non-nullable value type in order to use it as parameter 'T' in the generic type or method 'Nullable<T>'`
